text:
maya: quick Q — we're about to launch an A/B split that should only hit EU + paid tiers (pro/enterprise). Does smart-routing respect rollout.scope today or will fallback ignore the scope and send traffic to variants outside the scope?

sam: short answer: the router checks scope at assignment time, but fallback is a separate path and currently only looks at model compatibility and region, not customer_tier. so fallbacks can land in other tiers if the variant exists there.

dmitri: ugh, that matches my local repro. if variant B is only deployed to eu-pools, but fallback is to a quantized variant that we have globally, customers in EU paid get B but if capacity tight they get the global quantized fallback (which might be variant A-like). that can create cross-tier drift.

elena: is the concern that the rollout "cohort" loses identity after a fallback? we need to preserve the semantics: if user was picked for B, any fallback should prefer B-family variants first (even if quantized), then widen to other families.

maya: exactly. we don't want a paid EU customer in cohort B to suddenly get A outputs because of fallback ordering. also the console UI shows rollout % for "B in EU" and that would be misleading.

sam: proposed fix: add a cohort tag to the request context (rollout_id + variant family) and make the fallback scoring prefer same family variants with lower compatibility cost. minimal router change: when evaluating fallbacks, pass cohort tag and a bias to score variants that match family/scope.

dmitri: that sounds reasonable. edge case: what if family B doesn't have any compatible quantized kernels for that HW type? then we still should avoid sending to A if the cohort explicitly opted into B — maybe honor a policy flag like allow_cross_family_on_capacity: false for per-tier canaries.

elena: console/ux: need a toggle for "strict cohort isolation" per rollout. default false (to avoid hard outages) but for paid tiers we'd enable it. UI change + api flag rollout.strict_cohort_isolation (bool).

maya: agree. telemetry: we should emit a metric when cohort assignment != final_variant_family so we can alert on silent drift: rollout.route_mismatch.

sam: adding dto for router change, sample config:
```json
{
  "route_policy": "smart",
  "scope": {"regions": ["eu"], "tiers": ["pro","enterprise"]},
  "fallback": ["variant_v2_quant","variant_v1"],
  "strict_cohort_isolation": true
}
```

dmitri: implementation details — router already has scope evaluation and fallback list. new work: propagate rollout_id + family into request metadata + change fallback comparator to prefer same-family candidates and respect strict_cohort_isolation. also add a short-circuit to deny cross-tier fallback if flag = true.

elena: on console side we'll show an indicator on rollout timeline when strict_cohort_isolation is enabled and a per-tier "fallback rate" graph. ops can set alerts on rollout.route_mismatch > 0.5% in first 30m.

deploy-bot: canary v2-started for rollout=ab-eu-paid at 2024-11-02T14:22:45Z (5%).

maya: ok i'll open a tiny RFC and a router PR. anyone want to pair on the comparator logic?

sam: i'll pair tomorrow morning. leaving a note to test with mixed quantized + non-quantized variants across regions.

dmitri: i'll add a unit test that simulates capacity shortage and asserts cohort-prefers-family behavior.

elena: i'll draft the console change and mock the new metric.

maya: thanks team :thumbsup:
